notes: Breadboard hole names follow the catalogue convention (top half = bank 't', rows a-e; bottom half = bank 'b', rows f-j). The image labels the top half j-f and the bottom half e-a, so the row letters here are mapped by physical position. Only the strip (column + bank) matters electrically.

Column numbers and rail hole positions were estimated from the image: 5V wire at tp.2, GND wire at tn.3, rail-to-button wire at tp.5, rail-to-resistor wire at tn.10, rail-linking wires at column 29 (black) and 30 (red).

The two analog sensors are drawn as FSRs. Their legs go straight into the breadboard: one to the + rail (bp.4 / bp.12), the other to the divider column (6b / 16b), where a 10k resistor goes to the bottom - rail and a yellow wire goes to A0 / A1.

Pushbutton legs straddle the centre gap in columns 5 and 7. Column 5 top strip is fed 5V and column 7 top strip goes to pin 2 and the 10k pull-down resistor, which runs to GND via column 10. The assignment of the button's 1.l/1.r/2.l/2.r ports to the four legs is assumed.
Resistor value is given as 10000 ohms (10k).
The Arduino GND wire goes to the second GND pin next to the power header (GND.2).
